meta.title: Robotics Has Advanced Beyond Our Expectations | Big Ideas 2026 Mid-Year Review
meta.thread_line: 4 threads · robotaxis cross the safety bar · drone delivery scales · humanoids still early · SpaceX IPO and orbital compute

snapshot: ARK's mid-year update to its Big Ideas 2026 embodied-AI and space research, covering robotaxis, drone delivery, humanoids and reusable rockets.
Robotaxis: Waymo at 500,000+ driverless weekly rides targeting 1 million; ARK says Waymo is now safer than the US average accident rate.
Tesla robotaxi runs in seven regions and the Cybercab (no wheel, no pedals) is coming off the production line; Waymo is in 14 cities.
Drone delivery is live: Zipline passed 2.5M deliveries, Walmart passed 1M, DoorDash launched an in-house program.
Humanoids: ~20,000 humanoids and ~40,000 quadrupeds built so far; ARK sees a $20T+ market but calls it far earlier than autonomous driving.
SpaceX IPO'd at just under $2T raising ~$85B; ARK says it has a 10-year lead and cut launch costs ~95% since 2008.
SpaceX's S-1 centres on orbital AI data centers: a $28.5T TAM (90%+ AI) and a 2032 up-mass target ~1,000x the whole industry's 2025 total.

themes.status: SAFETY BAR CROSSED — NOW A SCALING RACE
themes.title: Robotaxis are safer than human drivers; the open question is how fast they scale
themes.lead: ARK says robotaxis already beat the national human accident rate, so adoption now depends on scale and price, not safety.
bullets: Waymo completes over 500,000 driverless rides per week and intends to scale to 1 million; it is in 14 cities after adding about nine this year.
Based on Waymo's disclosures, ARK says its police-reported crash rate is below the US average, and robotaxis are far safer on injury and worst-crash measures.
Tesla operates robotaxi in seven regions (about five added this year); Daniel tested it in Tampa last week and called it seamless.
Tesla is rolling the Cybercab, a purpose-built robotaxi with no steering wheel, pedals or wing mirrors, off the production line; officials have said cars without pedals or wheels will be allowed.
Tesla's customer cars act as mini R&D centers whose cameras collect accident and road data worldwide, which ARK calls an unparalleled data advantage.

Ride-hail costs about $2+/mile in Western markets versus ~$0.50/mile or less in China, so Chinese players (Baidu, WeRide, Pony AI) are moving to the Middle East and Europe where pricing is higher; ARK is focused on the US and Western markets.
Zoox also received recent regulatory approvals.

themes.title: Drone delivery is operating at scale and big platforms are verticalizing
themes.lead: Autonomous delivery is already running, and ARK expects drone delivery to push the delivery fee toward about a dollar or zero.
bullets: Zipline passed 2.5 million cumulative autonomous deliveries and is scaling its smaller Platform 2 drone for residential delivery (Platform 1 served medical deliveries in Africa).
Walmart passed 1 million autonomous drone deliveries, mostly Zipline plus Alphabet's Wing; it targets 270 locations covering over 40 million Americans by 2027.
DoorDash announced an in-house drone program last week and received FAA Part 135 certification, which allows airline-like drone operations.
Manna is scaling in the US after starting in Ireland; Meituan is scaling in China and the Middle East; Amazon sits at the bottom of the chart despite announcing drones decades ago.
The average US food delivery order is about $30, roughly half of it fees and markups; ARK thinks drones cut delivery cost to about $1 or less, likely folded into the item price like free shipping.

themes.title: Humanoids: huge market, but far harder and earlier than autonomous driving
themes.lead: ARK sees a $20 trillion-plus humanoid market, yet the gap between robots produced and robots deployed with customers is the metric that matters.
bullets: Cumulative production is roughly 40,000 quadrupeds and 20,000 humanoids, with many more unlisted makers; China has hundreds of humanoid manufacturers.
ARK sizes humanoids at $20T+, split between home robots and manufacturing.
Past ARK research estimates humanoids are 200,000x more complex than fully autonomous driving.
Data is harder to get: public roads allow driving data collection, but factory data requires being inside the factory long before the robot is useful.

Today's robots mostly dance, greet people in lobbies or chat like an LLM rather than do complex physical tasks; the supply chain still has to be built, and Tesla has said it is an entirely new product that will scale slowly.
Figure recently published a couple of demo videos; ARK wants to see customer deployments instead of production-count announcements.
themes.watch: Production counts are company announcements; ARK says the commercialization point is how many are actually deployed with customers.

themes.title: SpaceX IPO, reusability dominance and the orbital AI data center thesis
themes.lead: ARK says SpaceX has a 10-year lead, and the Starship-enabled orbital AI buildout is what underpins its IPO story.
bullets: SpaceX IPO'd at just under $2 trillion in value, raising roughly $85B.
SpaceX landed an orbital-class booster in 2015; Blue Origin matched it in 2025 and China has since joined the group.
ARK estimates SpaceX cut launch costs about 95% since 2008; it holds roughly two-thirds of all active satellites.
Starlink is close to 11,000 active satellites and over 12 million subscribers, growing weekly.
The S-1 cites a $28.5T total addressable market, over 90% AI related, built on orbital data centers (AI satellites rebranded Star Mind).
Up-mass to orbit passed 3,000 metric tons in 2025; SpaceX projects launching about 1,000x that in 2032 (nearly 2.5 million tons) to support a million satellites.
SpaceX discontinued the Falcon 9 rideshare program to focus on Starship, opening the small/medium launch category to others.

Some satellite providers struggle to book launch for 2028-2029+ after the Blue Origin explosion in May; Rocket Lab announced it intends to acquire Iridium, showing the value of owning both launch and payload.
themes.watch: SpaceX's up-mass and TAM figures are the company's own S-1 projections; ARK says Starship development is critical to the thesis and will be tracked through year-end.

takeaways.title: Track Waymo's weekly rides toward 1 million and Tesla's city count as the scaling scoreboard.
Weigh robotaxi exposure by pricing power: ARK favors the US and West over China's ~$0.50/mile market.
Watch Walmart's drone rollout (270 locations by 2027) and DoorDash's in-house program for delivery-fee compression.
Judge humanoid names on customer deployments, not units produced.
Follow Starship development; it gates the orbital data center story behind the SpaceX IPO.

hot_takes.take: Robotaxi is already safer than humans. Now it's just a matter of how quickly will it take to scale and expand the service.
hot_takes.why: Flat safety claim, ARK on the hook

We believe SpaceX has a 10-year lead on the industry.
Drone delivery could lower the price of delivery to just around a dollar or less.
